objectives.trace-authentication: Trace a claimed identity through credential verification to an authenticated actor.
objectives.evaluate-access: Evaluate an access decision for an actor, action and resource using authoritative policy inputs.
objectives.distinguish-actors: Distinguish the represented actor, the request sender and the principal used by Spring Security.
objectives.assign-responsibility: Explain who verifies proof, who asserts identity and who guards the protected resource.
objectives.compare-request-paths: Compare human and workload requests and diagnose a denial without expanding permissions.

sections.title: Separate an identity from its proof

practice.prompt: At 02:13 the request contains Maya’s account name. The backend has received no proof for it. What fact could it safely record?

choices.label: An account name was claimed.
choices.reason: The name tells the server which account is being claimed. A claimed field can be logged only if policy allows it, and it must be labelled as unverified.

choices.label: Maya signed in successfully.
choices.reason: That would record an authentication result before evidence was verified.

choices.label: Maya had permission to export.
choices.reason: The request has established neither a verified caller nor an access decision.

sections.title: Name the actor at each boundary

practice.prompt: A sign-in attempt returned a generic failure. Which diagnostic event would you keep?

choices.label: request_id=r-14 stage=authentication outcome=failed
choices.reason: This records the stage and outcome without storing the proof or implying a verified actor.

choices.label: request_id=r-14 submitted_password=<captured value>
choices.reason: A submitted password is secret material. Avoid storing it in diagnostic logs even when authentication fails.

choices.label: request_id=r-14 verified_actor=maya
choices.reason: No verified actor was established. The claimed account cannot be promoted to an authenticated identity in the audit record.

sections.title: Decide access to a specific resource

practice.prompt: Baseline: Maya is authenticated, has task:read, and belongs to North. Task 17 is in North. Change one input, then predict the result before running it.

choices.label: Move task 17 to South.
choices.reason: Denied · scope check. The read grant is unchanged, but the task’s stored workspace no longer matches Maya’s.

choices.label: Replace task:read with task:create.
choices.reason: Denied · action check. The task stays in North. A create grant does not permit reading an existing task.

choices.label: Change Maya’s display name.
choices.reason: Allowed · both checks still pass. The policy uses trusted authority and membership, not a mutable display label.

practice.prompt: The task API accepts the exporter’s verified identity but denies its read of a South task. Where do you investigate first?

choices.label: The task API’s policy inputs.
choices.reason: The API owns the access decision. Compare its trusted grants and the actual resource scope before changing permissions.

choices.label: The exporter’s sign-in secret.
choices.reason: Verified identity already reached the API. Rotating a secret does not explain an authorization denial.

choices.label: The deployment location of the identity verifier.
choices.reason: Moving the verifier does not change which component enforces policy or what scope the task belongs to.

sections.title: Follow a person and a workload

practice.prompt: The deployment audit says Maya deployed the exporter. At 02:13 the exporter calls the API with its own workload proof. Which identity goes in the verified runtime actor field?

choices.label: The verified exporter identity.
choices.reason: That is the caller established for this request. Keep Maya separately as the deployment actor.

choices.label: Maya’s human account.
choices.reason: Deployment ownership is a separate event. It does not establish intent, delegation or runtime identity.

choices.label: The task API identity.
choices.reason: The API is the receiver on this hop. It can have its own identity on a different outgoing call.

overnight-trace.title: Incident review · Two reads, one familiar name

items.detail: Maya reads Task 17 in North through the dashboard.
The exporter requests Task 17. A dashboard audit view shows Maya’s name again.

items.label: User
items.detail: Maya, the human operating the dashboard.

items.label: Subject
items.detail: The entity described by the statement under review. In Maya’s sign-in, that is Maya’s account.

items.label: Principal
items.detail: The application’s representation of the verified caller.

items.label: Client
items.detail: The software sending the request on this hop. It can be the dashboard calling the task API.

access-path.title: Signing in opens the policy decision

items.label: Claim + proof
items.detail: The dashboard looks up the account and verifies the submitted evidence.

items.label: Verified actor
items.detail: The request can now be evaluated as Maya.

items.label: Actor and action
items.detail: Maya asks to read Task 17 and has task:read.

items.label: Resource and scope
items.detail: Task 17 belongs to North. Permit the read only if the stored workspace matches Maya’s membership.

trust-path.title: Follow the request across the trust boundary

items.label: Receive the evidence
items.detail: The sign-in entry point receives the claimed account and its proof. The request fields are still caller-supplied.

items.label: Verify the actor
items.detail: A local verifier checks the proof. If a deployment accepts an external assertion, the provider makes it and the receiving application validates it.

items.label: Evaluate access
items.detail: The task API uses a trusted actor, the action, and the resource’s stored workspace. An identity claim cannot decide that scope.

items.label: Enforce the decision
items.detail: The resource boundary releases the task only when policy allows it. This responsibility still exists when verifier and resource API share a process.
Verified actor: Maya’s human account · Action: read task · Scope: North.
Deployment actor: Maya’s human account · Action: deploy exporter.
Verified actor: the exporter’s workload account · Action: read task · Scope: North.
